Subject: HealthSys - PII handling for prompts/outputs (post-call recap)

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side related to the PII/data handling questions you raised: 

1) What we store by default
   - Prompts: by default, prompt text is logged for telemetry and debugging for hosted API customers.
   - Outputs: generated outputs are also logged for the same purposes.
   - Metadata: request metadata (timestamps, model/version, region) is retained for observability.

2) Retention and access
   - Hosted default retention: 30 days for full request/response logs, then deleted from our hot storage. Aggregated telemetry is kept longer for product metrics.
   - Dedicated/Private: retention is configurable and can be set to meet contractual/legal requirements (including indefinite retention on customer-managed infra).

3) Residency and segmentation
   - For hosted: data is stored in the region you select (we discussed US-West (us-west-2) today).
   - Dedicated/Private options allow on-prem or VPC-only storage and avoid cross-region replication.

4) Controls and options
   - No-logs mode: available for Dedicated and Private deployments; we can also offer a hosted opt-out where logs are not retained beyond immediate processing (subject to contract).
   - Redaction & de-id: we provide SDK helpers and optional in-line redaction. We also recommend client-side pre-processing for sensitive fields.
   - Audit logs & SOC 2: our SOC 2 summary attached; full audit logs can be made available for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Action items
   - I'll follow up with a concise one-page summary (attached) and a recommended config for a 30-day retention policy in your chosen region.
   - Rishi is looping in on contractual language we discussed (PO/contract changes for retention and residency).

Can you confirm whether HealthSys prefers: (A) hosted with 30-day retention in us-west-2, (B) hosted with hosted-opt-out (limited logs) + addendum, or (C) Dedicated/Private?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up with your security team if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we move to procurement: 

- When you say prompts are logged for telemetry, is that the raw prompt text or a hashed/de-identified form by default?
- Are outputs stored in a way that our end-users could be re-associated to responses (e.g., user IDs or IPs in the logs)?
- If we choose hosted with 30-day retention, can you confirm where backups/replicas are located and whether they cross into other regions?
- For compliance, our security team will need the specific retention timeline in writing and a statement on whether Redwood processes or stores any PII outside the selected region.

Also, can you confirm whether any admin/engineering at Redwood can read the logs during troubleshooting, and if so, what controls/audit trails are in place?

samira.khan@healthsys.com

Hi Samira —

Great questions — see answers below and an attached one-page summary. I tried to be concise; happy to expand or provide a security-only doc for your team.

- Prompt logging: for hosted accounts, we store the raw prompt text in request logs by default (this is how we link prompts to traces for debugging). We offer two alternatives: (1) redaction via SDK (client-side) before sending, or (2) hosted opt-out where logs are not persisted beyond immediate processing. Dedicated/Private deployments default to not persisting logs unless the customer enables them.

- Association to users: by default we do not store end-user identifiers (we only keep request-level metadata). If your integration sends user IDs, those are present in logs. We recommend tokenizing or hashing any user identifiers client-side if you want to avoid association.

- Backups/replicas & residency: hosted backups are kept in the selected region (us-west-2) for the retention period. We do not replicate logs to other regions unless you enable multi-region replication. Our DR procedures may involve temporary cross-region transfers under controlled conditions—this is covered in our data handling addendum.

- Access controls & auditing: only authorized SRE/Support engineers with Just-In-Time access can access raw request logs for debugging. Access is logged in our audit system; we provide exported audit trails on request for Dedicated/Private customers and include audit logs as part of our SOC 2 evidence.

- Retention confirmation (hosted): default 30 days. We can add a stronger contractual SLT for 30 days with a requirement to purge beyond that window; we can also support shorter retention on request.

Next steps I propose:
  1) I'll send a short security appendix (focused on prompts/outputs, retention, residency, and access) — aiming to have that to you by end of day.
  2) Rishi will follow up on contractual language and addendum options (we can include hosted opt-out or Dedicated terms).
  3) If your security team wants a live session, I can coordinate a 20–30 minute call this week.

Rishi — adding you so you can confirm contract addendum language options for retention/residency.

Regards,
Marissa
